newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICAN STOCKS END SOFT ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICAN STOCKS END SOFT ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared midday losses but still ended soft on Monday in lackluster trade as investors took profits from recent market gains and sold stocks amid rising U.S. long bond yields.
The leading IPC index of 37 shares fell 31.40 points, or 0.69 percent, to 5,043.65. Volume was a weak 57 million shares.

Traders said the market's weakness was due just to profit-taking, but analysts said some investors were also nervous about rising long-term U.S. interest rates ahead of U.S. inflation data due out later this week.
"The profit-taking was normal after the market's gain," one dealer said.
Telephone company and market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico slipped 1.67 percent on profit-taking.
Also hit by profit-taking were shares of financial group Bancomer, which accounted for a third of all activity on the bourse. Its A shares fell 2.78 percent and its B shares slipped 0.79 percent.
Media firm Grupo Televisa escaped the day unharmed by gaining 3.56 percent. Shares gained after Mexican brokerage Banamex-Accival reiterated its buy rating on the company.
